title: Friendship Bracelets
statementMd:
UTPC is making friendship bracelets for an upcoming fair.

There are $n$ ($1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$) beads arranged in a row. The $i$-th bead has color $a_i$ ($1 \le a_i \le n$). A bracelet consists of a contiguous group of **at least two** beads, and the first and last beads in the bracelet must have the same color.

A bracelet containing $k$ beads earns $k$ dollars, but making a bracelet costs $c$ ($0 \le c \le 10^9$) dollars. You may make any number of bracelets, as long as no bead belongs to more than one bracelet. Beads not included in a bracelet earn nothing.

What is the maximum total profit you can earn? You may also choose to make no bracelets.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $c$ ($1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$, $0 \le c \le 10^9$), the number of beads and the cost of assembling one bracelet.

The second line contains $n$ integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ ($1 \le a_i \le n$), where $a_i$ is the color of the $i$-th bead.

## Output

Print one integer: the maximum possible total profit from making non-overlapping valid bracelets.

## Note

One optimal choice is to make a bracelet using beads at positions $1$ through $3$, and another using beads at positions $4$ through $8$. Their profits are $3-2=1$ and $5-2=3$, for a total of $4$. The last bead is unused.
